This message comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled
pros to get their home projects done well for over 30 years. For everything from minor repairs
to major remodels, find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton. The community of Bend, Oregon is grieving after
yesterday's shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School. The teenage shooter fired into a special
needs classroom. He killed three children, ages 5, 8, and 11, and a 25-year-old teacher,
Megan Lambert. Melanie Keebler is the mayor of Bend. It is just an incredible and profound moment
of grief and overwhelm for people. It's hard to process these kinds of things. It's unfathomable
that people would lose their children in this manner. When schools are supposed to be a place
where people can teach our children and they can feel safe. Police say a teacher threw her
phone at the gunman, then tackled and fought him, likely saving lives. He was shot dead by a man who
followed him into the building. The Trump administration is escalating its fight with
California, warning that local officials who process ballots submitted by suspected
non-citizen voters are putting themselves at risk of criminal investigation. The escalation comes
after the Trump administration sued the state to prevent it from counting mail-in ballots from
people the federal government has identified as likely non-citizens until their immigration
status can be confirmed. The Commerce Department's policy for scientific integrity no longer includes
language that bans political interference, as NPR's Hansi Lo Wang reports, the change has
implications for the U.S. Census. In a letter citing NPR's reporting, Democratic Senator Ron
Wyden of Oregon is demanding answers about why the Commerce Department removed internal policy
language that said, "Protection from inappropriate influence is among the hallmarks of scientific
integrity." Wyden says he's concerned that change hurts the credibility of official statistics from
the Census Bureau and other agencies under the Commerce Department. Senator Elizabeth Warren,
a Democrat from Massachusetts, has made a similar congressional inquiry. The Commerce Department
removed its ban on political interference in August after the Census Bureau released a highly
unusual document by a team with ties to the America First Policy Institute, a think tank started by
officials from President Trump's first administration. Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News. Ukrainian President
Volodymyr Zelensky is asking his European Union counterparts for more support heading into winter,
Terry Schultz reports. President Zelensky said he's counting on the EU for more assistance,
as his relationship with the Trump administration deteriorates. Russia continues to attack Ukraine's
energy infrastructure, and winter approaches. It's not only energy, it's also air defense and
funding, and I'm thankful that EU stands with us. Some EU leaders are reportedly pressing Zelensky
to rein in his criticism of Trump, but they're also concerned the U.S. ended its ban on Russian
diesel imports, earning Moscow money. EU leaders are again debating whether and how almost $250
billion worth of frozen Russian assets can be used to fund Ukraine. For NPR News, I'm Terry
Schultz in Brussels. Major U.S. stock indexes closed lower today. The S&P 500 lost more than
1 percent. The Nasdaq sank more than 2 percent. This is NPR. New York Mayor Zoran Mamdani and
city Democrats are urging private parking lot owners to block federal immigration officers
from using their properties. The plea follows the shooting of a 28-year-old during an arrest
last week. Federal officers had used a nearby private lot as a staging area. A Department
of Homeland Security spokesperson defended the agency's actions. Researchers are learning more
about how psychology influences the ability to bounce back from a sports injury. NPR's Will Stone
reports it's not just about being physically well enough to return to activity. A sizable share of
people, about one in three, who undergo ACL surgery don't return to their previous level of sport.
Fear of being re-injured is often a big reason. Shelby Bias directs the Psychology of Sports
Injury Lab at UNC Chapel Hill. In a new study, she and other researchers followed about 60 people
recovering from ACL surgery and ran a series of physical and psychological tests. It wasn't
necessarily those objective factors or quad strength and hop symmetry that were predictive
or associated with psychological readiness. In her work at UNC, Bias is finding that certain
approaches like mindfulness and grounding techniques can be helpful for people who are
cleared to play but still struggle with anxiety and fear after their injury. Will Stone, NPR News.
Brazil's government says that annual deforestation in the Amazon has fallen to its lowest level since
1988. The rainforest lost about 1,300 square miles from August 2025 through July 2026.
That's a lot less than it did during the surge under former President Jair Bolsonaro during
his presidency. Deforestation increased by about 60 percent. This is NPR. This message comes from
Cure Alzheimer's Fund. From family to community, connections and the memories they make are
everything. The hugs, the strolls, the laughs, songs and dreams. Cure Alzheimer's Fund empowers
the scientists who dedicate their lives to curing Alzheimer's disease. Great progress has been made
and the momentum is building. There is more to do. Learn more at curealz.org. Let's keep our memories together.

Trump administration escalates fight with California, warning local officials over ballots from suspected non-citizens
Commerce Department drops ban on political interference in scientific work, drawing Senate inquiries and Census concerns
Zelensky asks EU for more support heading into winter as Russia attacks Ukraine's energy infrastructure
Major U.S. stock indexes close lower, with the S&P 500 down over 1 percent and the Nasdaq off over 2 percent
New York Mayor Mamdani urges private parking lot owners to block federal immigration officers after shooting
Research finds psychology drives return to sport after ACL surgery, with fear of re-injury a major barrier
Brazil reports Amazon deforestation at lowest level since 1988 for August 2025 through July 2026
